title: diagnose delayed metadata propagation causing intermittent project mischarge
creator: Luis Moreno
description: Several customers have reported short windows (10-90s) of mischarged usage after API key rotations and subaccount rebinds. Symptoms: token exchanges succeed, requests are served, but consumption shows attributed to the old project for the first N requests after rotation. Root hypothesis: asynchronous metadata propagation (token->project mapping) to edge services lags behind traffic path activation, combined with stale in-memory claim cache on edge proxies causing a race during bind/unbind operations.
repro_steps: 1) Create subproject A and B, issue delegated API key for A
2) Start traffic through proxy X that has warm claim cache pointing at A
3) Rotate key or rebind that key to project B via control-plane API
4) Observe incoming requests still attributed to A for ~10-90 seconds in billing dashboard while control-plane reports B as owner
5) Confirm logs: control-plane emits mapping update event, kafka consumer processes but edge proxy caches were not invalidated or saw stale claim revision
investigation_notes: - Event pipeline: mapping updates published to topic 'claims.v2' with partitioning by token-id; our consumer group processes updates and writes to projection store (redis + local TTL cache in proxies).

- Found race: when control-plane marks token as active for new project, control-plane flips 'active_project' then emits event; sometimes the projection update is delayed during high throughput and consumer lag spikes coincide with key rotations.

- Edge proxies maintain a hot in-memory claim cache with 60s TTL and only listen to projection-change webhooks for immediate invalidation. In several incident traces the webhook delivery to the proxy failed (timeout) and the cache kept the old mapping.
- We reproduced locally by introducing a 200ms delay in the projection writer + dropping webhook deliveries: attribution flips only after cache TTL expiry.
- Rate-limiter counters are keyed by (project_id, rate_key). When attribution is stale, tokens get counted to previous project buckets causing quota bleed.
- No evidence tokens were accepted that should have been rejected; this is strictly attribution and quota/rate-limiter owner mapping, not authentication bypass.
- Existing reconciliation job runs nightly; window too large to catch short incidents and customers cannot wait for next-day corrective billing.
proposed_solution: Short term (hotfix): change proxy cache TTL from 60s to 5s for project claim entries and enable immediate webhook retry/backoff to ensure invalidations are delivered. Deploy to canary region first.

Mid term: make project claim updates atomic in control-plane: emit update with monotonic claim_revision and make projection consumers write claim_revision to projection store. Proxies must check claim_revision before serving attribution.

Long term: switch to versioned claim resolution where requests carry claim_revision header supplied by edge after a short startup handshake. On rotation, clients must fetch latest claim metadata before sending production traffic (SDK update).
Reconciliation: implement an intra-hour backfill that scans 5-minute windows around token changes and corrects meter entries visible to billing to give near-real-time fixes to affected customers.
Testing: add integration tests that simulate consumer lag, webhook failures, and validate final attribution correctness and rate-limiter bucket assignment.

Risk/Tradeoffs: reducing TTL increases control-plane traffic to proxies and may slightly increase latency; versioned claims require coordinated SDK and runtime changes and rollout planning across Dedicated/Private installs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary rollout with TTL=5s shows no misattribution incidents for rotations in canary region for 72h under synthetic churn
2) Projection consumers include claim_revision, and proxies compare revision before attributing—unit and integration tests cover the check
3) Backfill job implemented and can reconcile a sample 1-hour window end-to-end and produce corrected billing entries in staging
4) Alerting: create an SLA dashboard for consumer lag and webhook delivery failures and an oncall playbook added to runbook
5) Documentation updated: Confluence design doc and SDK guidance for graceful key handover

review_feedback: PM (Jonah Rivera): prioritize a customer-visible rollback plan and a communication template for affected customers
Security (Maya Chen): confirm no sensitive token contents are logged during repro; flagged need to scrub debug logs before sharing
Infra (Evan Gupta): suggested we use durable Kafka consumer group offsets stored in ZK to reduce consumer lag spikes and agreed to set higher IO priority for claims topic
Design (Priya Kothari): requested that UX for SDK key handover be explicit about recommended grace period and include code examples
